data.name: Shrivan
data.long_meaning: Shri is the Goddess of wealth, prosperity and abundance. Van is a prefix meaning 'forest' or 'abode'. Together, Shrivan can be interpreted as the 'God of the abundant forest' or the 'God of the prosperous abode'.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shrivan may reflect Indian cultural traditions associating deities with abundant natural resources, such as forests. This name could also symbolize wealth and prosperity within the community, as the name directly includes the invocation to Shri, the Goddess associated with wealth and abundance.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu tradition, Shrivan may be seen as a spiritual symbol of the abundant and thriving natural world, representing the bountiful gifts of nature that sustain all life. It also underscores the spiritual significance of recognizing and expressing gratitude for the material blessings and abundance in our lives. The name evokes a sense of connection to the Divine as the provider of all sustenance.

historical_references.reference: Shrivan was an important general in the army of the Chalukya king, Pulakeshin II, during the 7th century. He is best known for his victory over the Pallava king, Narasimhavarman II, in the Battle of Thothikonda.

Shrivan is also mentioned in the epic poem, the Mahabharata, as the son of Bhishma Pitamaha and Veda Prabha. He is described as a mighty warrior and one of the twelve Vasus, powerful deities who personify various natural elements.
